_comment: Machine-readable contract for document generation from ABAP source.
This file defines what docgen.py must produce and what checks/docgen.py must validate.
docgen.py generates documentation from ABAP source; checks/docgen.py validates the output.
Four document types are supported:
- report: full analysis report (existing report_qc.py validates this)
- class: technical documentation for ABAP classes
- table: table structure documentation from SELECT statements
- onboarding: onboarding guide for new developers
Each document type has its own required_sections and structure rules.
The gate_io rules define exit codes and refusal conditions.
1.0.1, shipped with 1.1.17, closed seven gaps found by re-reading the two scripts against this contract and running them.

validated_by named three flags that do not exist (--check-class, --check-table, --check-onboarding); argparse refused all three, and the real --validate flag appeared in no prose anywhere. Now the actual invocation.

--format html --validate failed its own output with five false missing-section defects. validate() had a format parameter defaulting to markdown and its only call site passed three arguments, so the HTML branch was unreachable and an HTML document was checked for markdown headings it cannot contain by construction.

load_contract() swallowed OSError and JSONDecodeError and returned {}, and an empty contract means no required sections and no validation flags, so --validate answered PASS against no rules. It now raises and main() refuses, the same way report_qc.py does for report-contract.json.
Three validation flags were decoration; they are now real switches defaulting to true.
A validation failure used to return before the write, leaving no document on disk; the document is written and rc carries the verdict.
Refusals printed error on stderr; report_qc.py prints it on stdout, so a caller reading one stream saw exit 2 with no message.
abap_deps_analyzer refused with exit 1, which this project reserves for the analysis ran and found defects. It now refuses with exit 2 and prints the same error prefix.

1.0.2 moves version because the contract now records what the seven validation flags actually do, and because the generator refuses three source shapes that used to end in a PASS about the wrong thing. A .md or .markdown source handed to docgen was parsed as ABAP and a fresh document generated about it, so --validate answered PASS for a document this tool never read; it now refuses and points at report_qc.py. A directory source was reported as not found, which sent a reader hunting for a filename; it now says it is a directory. An empty source produced a document about a program that does not exist and validated as PASS for --type onboarding and --type table; it now refuses. abap_deps_analyzer.py got the same treatment for a directory source: a directory used to fall through to its bare except and print the raw IsADirectoryError text, which names no role and matches no recorded refusal; it now says the source is a directory and was not analysed, on the same exit-2 path as missing dependencies. The flag table is unchanged; only validation._comment is new. ships_with moves to 1.1.18.

1.0.3 moves version and ships_with together, because the generator now refuses one more shape of contract. checks/docgen.py's load_contract() read the schema and returned it, and validate() assumed the shape: document_types as a number made contract.get("document_types", {}).get() raise AttributeError out of validate() and exit 1, the defect verdict, for a contract that was only reshaped. And a root object with no rules at all answered PASS against no required sections and no validation flags -- a verdict with nothing behind it, which is the false reassurance --validate exists not to give, and the one a reader would assume the 1.0.1 unreadable-contract refusal had already covered. load_contract() now checks presence and shape in the same call as the read, main() widened its catch to KeyError and TypeError alongside OSError and ValueError, and both refuse at the contract on the same line as the unreadable one. This is the guard checks/contract.py has carried for report-contract.json since 1.2.4, which the twin never got: the report contract's guard was widened at 1.1.24 and 1.3.11 and recorded in its own _comment, while this file had none at all. No rule and no flag moved; only the refusal and its record.

report.description: Full analysis report with six sections (validated by report_qc.py)

table.description: Table structure documentation from SELECT statements

exit_codes.0: document generated or validated successfully; validation passed
exit_codes.1: validation failed: the document was still written, rc carries the verdict. Before 1.0.1 the FAIL branch returned before the write, so a document that failed validation left nothing on disk to look at, and the caller had to guess what was wrong
exit_codes.2: refused to run: nothing was generated or validated. Prints error at column 0 on stdout, matching report_qc.py; before 1.0.1 it went to stderr, where a caller reading stdout saw exit 2 with no message. 1.0.3 adds the shaped-wrong contract above as a trigger: it prints the same cannot read the contract line, because the check runs in load_contract with the read, so there is nothing to distinguish it for

refusal_triggers: output path directory does not exist
output path directory is not writable

the contract cannot be read: schemas/docgen-contract.json is missing, unreadable or not parseable JSON. Before 1.0.1 checks/docgen.py swallowed this and returned an empty dict, so --validate checked the document against no rules at all and answered PASS
output path is a file rather than a directory, which mkdir reports as not writable

the contract parses but is shaped wrong: a root that is not an object, a missing document_types or validation, document_types or validation that is not an object, required_sections that is not a list, or a section with no string heading_anchor. Before 1.0.3 a root object with no rules at all answered PASS against no required sections and no flags, and document_types as a number raised AttributeError out of validate() and exited 1 -- the defect verdict, for a contract that was only reshaped

_comment: Every flag here is a real switch as of 1.0.1. Three were decorative before then: required_sections, encoding_utf8 and code_fences_closed appeared in this object while validate() read no caller of them, so the checks ran unconditionally and setting them to false did nothing. They now default to true, so behaviour is unchanged while the flag means what it says.

1.0.2 records the scope of each flag, which the table did not say. Only encoding_utf8 is read on every text format: it is checked before the format branch, so markdown and html both honour it. The other six -- required_sections, sections_exactly_once, code_fences_closed, no_line_numbers_in_labels, mermaid_safe and tables_well_formed -- sit after the html early return, so they apply to markdown alone; an html document is never checked for required sections, fences, tables or the rest. The json output is a separate code path, validate_json(), which reads none of the seven: it checks only a hardcoded list of four top-level fields plus the type-specific arrays, so toggling any flag here does not change json validation at all. Nothing was aligned, because there is no bug to fix -- the json shape has no headings, fences or tables to check -- but a caller who sets a flag expecting it to reach json will not be told.
